unite_adi: UPPER SECONDARY-PREP YEAR-LEVEL: B1 - THEME 14: LIFE IN THE WORLD AND CULTURE

bolumler.ogrenmeKanitlari: PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT: Students will design and write a project about their ideal world tour. In this project, they will focus on different capitals of countries, famous landmarks, and cultural differences in various cities. They will describe their ideal travel experiences, including the roles and activities of people in these cities. Students will write scripts for the characters representing different countries, landmarks, and local traditions. These characters will act out various scenarios and interactions to showcase cultural diversity and famous attractions. The assignment will be evaluated using rubrics. Öğrenme-Öğretme Yaşantıları
bolumler.temelKabuller: This theme includes the concept of ''life in the world and culture with its components such as capitals of countries; landmarks and famous places in capitals and cities; cultural differences in different parts of the world'' and it is assumed that it could be present in almost all languages, with some exceptions. It is assumed that a student in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school may know what capitals of countries; landmarks and famous places in capitals and cities; cultural differences in different parts of the world mean in their own language as it is known that almost all people who start to learn a new language bring their pre-existing knowledge (in their own language) with them and transfer it to their new language learning context. However, they may not know how to say these things in another language if this has not yet been covered in their existing curriculum. Fortunately, this existing knowledge in their own language can help them recognise, understand, and learn them more easily in a foreign language, in this case English. As they are students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school, they are expected to know some basic vocabulary about ''life in the world and culture'' in English from previous themes and/or years such as ''Canada, Germany, Spain, museum, historical and so on'' and also some structures such as ''You should visit the pyramids of Giza. They were walking around the Colosseum when it started to rain.'' in English from the previous themes and/or years. These grammar items and vocabulary are revised during the ''Revision Programme'' at the beginning of the year and they can be used as a basis for learning the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme, so that the new grammatical elements in the current theme can be learnt easily.
bolumler.onDegerlendirme: It is assumed that these students in the preparatory year of an upper secondary school are ready to learn the concept of ''capitals of countries; landmarks and famous places in capitals and cities; cultural differences in different parts of the world'' cognitively, affectively, and socially since it is appropriate to their age and language level. Therefore, a contextual poster or a large picture could be provided for the students to remember and practise the items that they are related and previously learnt so that they can discuss about the poster and/or the picture in pairs and write down what they remember. This session can help them revise all the related vocabulary and grammatical elements that they have already learnt from previous themes or from previous years as a preparatory practice. In this way, their performance can be evaluated in terms of how much they remember and how accurately they use these items to build their competence in the current theme. It can help the teacher decide what to emphasise, revise, and practise in order to facilitate the new vocabulary and grammatical items in the current theme. (Their performance can be evaluated by rubrics, a rating scale, and /or a marking scheme during these practices.).
bolumler.zenginlestirme: Objective: To identify capitals and their famous attractions in English by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar. Activity 1: Listening and Reporting on Capitals and Attractions Students listen to a recording about different capitals and their attractions in order (''First, Ankara and Anıtkabir, Paris and the Eiffel Tower, then London and Big Ben''.). Each student receives a worksheet with pictures of these places and writes numbers next to the pictures based on the order they hear. They listen a second time to gather detailed information, such as ''The Eiffel Tower represents Paris’s modern and iconic architecture''. Next, students write sentences in reported speech using the details, like ''The speaker said that the Eiffel Tower represents Paris’s modern and iconic architecture''. A third listening is done to check and add any missing information. Finally, students exchange worksheets with each other for peer correction, and the teacher provides feedback to improve the use of target grammar and target vocabulary. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
bolumler.destekleme: Objective: To identify capitals and their famous attractions in English by using the target vocabulary and the target grammar. Activity 1: The teacher prepares two sets of cards, either physical or digital (via a web 2.0 tool): one set with capitals (''Ankara, Paris, London'') and another with attractions (''Eiffel Tower, Big Ben''). Students match the cards, then take turns forming sentences such as, ''Paris is famous for the Eiffel Tower''. After a student says a sentence, the teacher points to that student and asks another student, ''What did [Student’s Name] say?''. The second student answers using reported speech, for example, ''He said that Paris is famous for the Eiffel Tower''. This continues until all matches are completed. Finally, the teacher gives supportive feedback after each response. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
